Architecture

Understanding LucidRAG's unified pipeline system and deployment options

Unified Pipeline Architecture

Unified Pipeline Diagram
Visual: File Upload → PipelineRegistry → Auto-route → 5 Pipelines → Embeddings + Entities + Evidence

Key Principles

  • • Unified IPipeline interface
  • • Auto-routing by file extension
  • • Signal-based architecture
  • • Priority-based execution (110 → 5)

5 Processing Pipelines

  • • DocumentPipeline (PDF, DOCX, etc.)
  • • ImagePipeline (22-wave analysis)
  • • DataPipeline (CSV, Excel, Parquet)
  • • AudioPipeline (transcription, speakers)
  • • VideoPipeline (scenes + audio)

Single Instance (Free Tier)

All-in-one deployment for small teams

Single Instance Diagram
Web App → Processing → Vector Store + GraphRAG

What You Get

  • All 5 pipelines running on one server
  • SQLite for metadata (standalone) or PostgreSQL (production)
  • InMemory vectors (standalone) or Qdrant (production)
  • Perfect for small teams and proof-of-concept

Distributed System (Paid Tier)

Horizontal scaling for production workloads

Distributed System Diagram
Load Balancer → Web App → Message Queue → [Ingesters + Searchers] → Clustered Storage

What You Get

  • Horizontal scaling across multiple servers
  • Separate ingester and searcher services
  • Queue-based job distribution
  • Clustered vector stores and GraphRAG
  • Fault tolerance and high availability

Multi-Tenant Architecture

Schema-per-tenant isolation for enterprise

Multi-Tenant Diagram
LucidRAG Instance → [tenant_acme schema + qdrant:acme_vecs] + [tenant_globex schema + qdrant:globex_vecs]

Features

Schema-per-Tenant

Complete PostgreSQL schema isolation for each tenant

Auto-Provisioning

Tenant schemas created automatically on first access

Domain Routing

Subdomain or path-based routing (acme.lucidrag.com)

Per-Tenant Vector Collections

Separate Qdrant collections for each tenant

RBAC

Role-based access control per tenant
